Relatives will likely see this first (if they enter the prayer room), and it’s non-negotiable for the festival’s meaning. - **HOW:** - Place 1-3 diya ( oil lamp) on the prayer altar or a clean cloth. - **Use * only* clean, dry cotton wicks** (no paper or unsafe materials). - Fill with * clean oil* ( sesame or coconut oil work best). **- *Light them immediately* before relatives arrive** ( oil diyas need fresh lighting daily for safety and symbolism). - **SAFETY TIP:** Keep away from curtains, fabric, or children’s reach. Use a small tray underneath to catch spills. - *Skip this?* **Don’t** – it’s the heart of Diwali. If you only do one thing, make this it. --- ### ✨ **Priority #2: Entrance & Main Living Area Diyas (10-15 mins)** - **WHY:** Guests will * first step into your home*. A welcoming diya at the entrance and in the main living area sets the tone for warmth and celebration. - **HOW:** - **Front door:** Place 2- diya on a small table, shelf, or even a clean stone * outside* the door (if safe from wind). - **Inside the main room:** Group 3- diya on a central table, near the sofa, or on a sideboard. - **Pro tip:** Use * electric diya* ( LED) if you’re short on time or have kids/pets – they’re safer and no oil prep needed! - **SAFETY TIP:** Avoid placing diya near flammable items ( curtains, paper decorations, or fabric). - *Skip this?* **No** – it’s the " first impression" for Diwali. Guests will * feel* the light even if other decorations are minimal. --- ### ✨ **Priority #3: Dining Table Diyas (5 mins)** - **WHY:** Relatives will eat together – diya on the dining table ensures the * shared meal* is lit with sacred light ( a key Diw ritual). - **HOW:** - 2- diya on a small centerpiece ( e.g., a flower arrangement or a decorative bowl). - **Use short diya** so they don’t block views or conversation. - **SAFETY TIP:** If using oil diya, place them on a heat-resistant tray. - *Skip this?* **Only if absolutely no time** – but it’s quick and meaningful. --- ### ✨ **What to * defer* ( do these * after* diyas are lit):** - **Rangoli:** If you have time, do a * simple* one at the entrance ( using flour or colored sand – 15 mins max). - ** fairy lights:** String them * only* in visible areas ( e.g., along a shelf or window) – not the entire house. - **Wall decorations:** Focus on 1- key areas ( e.g., a small Diwali poster near the prayer room). - **" perfect" clean-up:** Tidy * only* high-visibility zones ( living room, dining area, entrance). Guests won’t notice a slightly messy kitchen if the main areas are warm and lit. --- ### 💡 **Key Tips to Save Time & Stay Safe:** - **Use electric diya if you’re stressed** – they’re flameless, reusable, and no oil prep. Many stores sell them for ₹50-₹100. - **" done is better than perfect"** – relatives will * love* the effort, not a Pinterest-perfect setup. A few well-placed diya with a " happy Diwali" sign is more meaningful than a cluttered house. - ** involve family:** Assign tasks ( e.g., " can you arrange diya on the dining table while I light the prayer room?"). - ** safety first:** Never leave oil diya unattended. Keep a fire extinguisher or water nearby. - ** last-minute touch:** A bowl of fresh flowers or a few candles on a windowsill ( if using electric) adds instant warmth in 5 mins. > **" Diwali is about light, not perfection. A single diya in the prayer room, one at the entrance, and one on the dining table will make your home feel sacred and welcoming – and that’s all that matters."** > > **You’ve got this!** Start with the prayer room diya * right now* – it’s the most meaningful step.
